text: THE PRIME MINISTER'S QUOTE MATCHES THE DESIGN IT WAS DRAWN FROM. The card stood on a pale-blue band, which put a third ground between the hero photograph and the card and read as a seam rather than a section; the Figma frame's gradient is switched off in the file, so the card now sits on the page's own white with 32 above and below, as drawn. It gains the 1px peach hairline the design gives it — bound to the nearest published secondary rung, because the drawn #FFC1BC is off the ramp and no border/brand/secondary rung exists. The quotation mark was a 64px Material `format_quote` at full strength, which is a CLOSING mark standing above the words; it is now the design's own vector, exported from the card rather than approximated, at 128 behind the first line at 40% — not an <Icon> because Material publishes no opening mark and the icon scale tops out at 64. The photograph is the design's too: a portrait in a navy jacket stood on the saffron panel where the design places a saffron one, and it now fills the panel edge to edge as drawn instead of floating as a contained cut-out. Its resolution is the open item, and the design says so itself — the layer is named "PM Photograph (DBIM Toolkit — pending)" and the source is 488x409 against a 351px panel, shipped at its own size rather than upscaled. The quote column takes the design's deeper top padding and its 24 above the attribution rule. On a phone the mark scales to keep the design's mark-to-type ratio, and the portrait caps at 240 — at 320 it stood 340px tall and outweighed the quotation it belongs to.
